# Save applications: Discord

**Pattern:** Form Intake · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Form

## Overview

Starts when the form is submitted, and covers newsletters work end to end across Discord and Notion.

It moves through 11 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. New Email Form Submission
2. Normalize Email Payload
3. Route by Work Type
4. Process 'sales' → Notion
5. Fast-Track 'support' + Alert
6. Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
7. Merge Routed Work
8. Guard Non-Empty from
9. Stamp Processing Time
10. Save Execution Metadata
11. Send Summary to Discord

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing newsletters work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

New Email Form Submission → Normalize Email Payload → Route by Work Type → Process 'sales' → Notion → Fast-Track 'support' + Alert → Hold Unknown Types (DLQ) → Merge Routed Work → Guard Non-Empty from → Stamp Processing Time → Save Execution Metadata → Send Summary to Discord → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Discord and Notion aligned by hand for newsletters
- Intake checked for completeness before it is stored in Discord, for newsletters
- Newsletters work where "Normalize Email Payload" is still a manual step before Discord
- Newsletters work that only reaches Discord when a form is submitted, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Discord and Notion in step for newsletters, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Discord or Notion call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 13 nodes in this newsletters build
- Branches rejoin before Discord, so a newsletters run reports once rather than 13 times
- Every newsletters run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Discord
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 13 nodes for newsletters before wiring Discord

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Discord webhook URL; Notion integration token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Unrecognized work types are parked in a dead-letter lane instead of erroring the whole run or silently dropping the item — new event kinds will show up eventually, and this is where you'd notice one without losing it. One kind is deliberately routed through a sub-workflow to show how heavier per-type logic can be extracted without touching this router at all.

## Practice exercises

Once it's wired up with real credentials, try:

1. Send a work-type value that matches no switch rule and confirm it lands in the dead-letter branch.
2. Add a new work type and its own handling branch.
3. Replace the direct-write branch with a sub-workflow call, matching the pattern already used for the first kind.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.
_Gotcha:_ Webhook mode needs no bot token. Messages cap at 2000 characters.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your newsletters process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Discord: give the bot access to the destination channel only, not the whole guild.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.

**Do not log**
newsletters payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
